"And what's wrong with that?" the man leaned back, eyes still on the road ahead. "Freedom of speech... freedom of arms... it applies everywhere, right?"

"No," said Sarah, setting her water bottle down on the passenger seat. She turned to him, a grim smile tugging at the corner of her mouth. "That is the specific problem. When you walk up to the border, you aren't walking into your country anymore. You're walking into a different sovereign nation with completely different laws."

She paused for effect, watching his hands tighten around the steering wheel.

"He was arrested," she continued. "Not detained. Arrested. He spent four days in the facility while the RCMP tried to figure out why exactly he thought he had the authority to carry a loaded handgun on Canadian soil. His lawyers were baffled. His parents were terrified."

The driver exhaled slowly through his nose, shifting into low gear at a red light. "So, no entry?"

"The gun was confiscated, obviously. He was processed, fingerprinted, and charged with possession of a firearm contrary to the Firearms Act, which is an indictable offense."

"But then," he insisted, pointing a thumb toward the sky. "Then they have to ask him questions about the Second Amendment."

"I think they actually asked him what he meant by 'given to him by God,' though," Sarah interrupted softly. "I mean, the officer's job is security, not theology. The guy walked in shouting constitutional rights to a customs agent, and suddenly everyone knows you don't want to deal with that on a Tuesday morning."

He pulled into the driveway and stopped the car. "Did he ever pay the money?"

"We heard from him yesterday," Sarah said. "He got the fines, he lost the ammo, and he had to surrender the weapon permanently. But worst of all?"

"What?"

"He spent the whole flight back here apologizing to the pilot for the delay."

Sarah opened her door to step out, turning the ignition key in her own car once more before shaking her head. "It's not about the law, Dave. It's about respect. He could have been polite. He could have said, 'I believe in my rights.' But instead, he treated the border like a theme park attraction where the only rule was to shout until you won something."

Das Licht des Schreibtischmonitors blendete Anna, als sie die Augen öffnete. Ein seltsames Echo eines Windgeschlurres hatte ihre Träume geziert, ein lautes Brüllen von Hirschgeweihen unter dem lauten Krachen von Baumästen. Sie war tief in ihren eigenen Schweiß getaucht gewesen, doch als sie jetzt hier stand, das Haar durcheinander und die Schultern steif von einem Schlaf, der nichts kostbareres war als Luft, fühlte sich alles zu flüchtig und zu real an. Die Decke war noch nicht heruntergefallen, denn das Glas der Bürostube brannte hell.

„Na, hallo Maus!"

Lukas tippte gegen die Glasscheibe ihres kleinen Arbeitsplatzes, hinter ihm stand Markus mit einem Lächeln, das weniger freundlich aussah als schadenfroh. Anna zögerte kurz, dann hob sie den Kopf. Ihre Wangen glühend heiß, spürte sie plötzlich, wie sich die Luft um ihre Taille zusammenzog, als hätte jemand die Temperatur in diesem winzigen Raum erhöht.

„Ich..." Anna begann, doch die Stimme versagte kurz den Dienst. Sie wollte etwas sagen, vielleicht nur eine Entschuldigung für das kurze Nicken, das statt einer Begrüßung kam. Doch Lukas sah es anders.

„Du hast uns geweckt, Anna. Mit dieser... Jagdphantasie von dir."

Die Worte hingen schwer in der Luft, wie Rauch von einem erstickten Feuer. Sie kannten den Stoff ihrer Fantasien nicht, aber sie kannten auch nicht wirklich Anna. Nur dass sie dort saß, drei Jahre lang, nie mehr als eine Zeile in einer Präsentation oder eine Kopierleistung in einem Team. In ihren Köpfen war sie nicht die einsame Frau, die abends stundenlang allein im dunklen Korridor nach Hause ging, sondern eine Exotik, die nur auf den Bildern im Internet erschien, die Markus manchmal postete. Er lachte leise, während er sich neben dem Fenster drehte.

„Weißt du, ich glaube, du brauchst mal was anderes als nur Arbeit in deinem Leben", sagte ein weiterer Kollege, der sich gerade aus einem Treffen zurückgezogen hatte. „Vielleicht solltest du deinen Traum leben. Eine wilde Treibjagd klingt doch toll. Mehr als das Hier-Sein."

Anna wollte entkräften, dass sie kein Tier jagte, sondern eher gefangen wurde in diesen Gedankenmustern, aber ihre Lippen waren schwer von der Hitze, die ihr innere Welt durchflutet hatte. Als würde die Gesellschaft selbst ein Signal senden, dass sie etwas falsch gemacht hatte, trat sie vom Stuhl weg, um zur Kaffeemaschine zu gehen. Dort stand sie nun still vor dem Geräusch des Wasserdampfes und den metallischen Klängen der Kapseln, die niemand sonst hören konnte, aber deren Schlägelklingen sich in ihren Ohren hallten.

Es war Freitag, die Zeit war so knapp geworden, dass Anna kaum merkte, dass die Sonne bereits unten lag. Der Rest des Teams machte sich bereit für die Abendessenpartien oder das Wochenende. Die meisten Kollegen trugen ihre Jacken über die Schulter, strahlten die Leichtigkeit eines freien Abends aus.

„Bleib einfach länger dran, ja?" rief Marcus von hinten, als die Tür des Raumes geöffnet wurde und er seinen Rucksack über die Schulterwarf. Anna nickte nur. Ihr Blick fiel auf den Stapel Dokumente auf ihrem Tisch, die eigentlich heute schon fertig sein sollten, aber nun lagen da noch drei weitere Abschnitte, die dringend erledigt werden mussten.

Sie setzte sich wieder hin. Der Bildschirm leuchtete auf ihr, der Text blinkte, doch ihre Gedanken waren noch immer an das Gefühl gekoppelt, das sie beim Aufwachen gespürt hatte. Ein warmer Fluss in ihrem Körper, der sie nicht losließ, der wie ein Gedanke blieb, auch wenn sie versuchte, ihn zu ignorieren.

„Ach, Anna, vergiss nicht, wir wünschen dir einen schönen Abend!", rief jemand von außen, lächelnd. Es klang, als wäre es eine Festlichkeit.

Anna lächelte zurück, obwohl sie wusste, dass ihre Einsamkeit keine Antwort finden würde. Sie arbeitete weiter, bis die Nacht in grauen Nebeln endete. Draußen war es kalt, aber hier drinnen wurde es wärmer, je mehr Zeit verging, während sie sich fragte, ob die Realität jemals so intensiv war wie diese Träume.

Als die anderen gegangen waren, blieb sie mit der Arbeit stehen. Die Lampen wurden gedimmt, der Schatten des Tisches fiel auf ihre Stirn. Sie legte die Hand auf den Schreibtisch und starrte auf den Punkt im Monitor, der nun leuchtete wie ein Auge, das sie beobachtete.

Just to hear a voice, to see where she begin.

With a story in hand, left to be hide.
Mrs. Vex looked confused at the screen,
As if she'd been hit by a meteorite scene.
The highest expectations were clearly too high,
For six-year-olds who just wanted to fly.

As Momma Linda sent a note through the wing.
"Don't ask them to be grown-ups yet,"
"Unless you want to teach them how to eat!"

这是一份为您定制的玄幻题材项目策划书及剧本片段。由于“小说”与“影视剧本”在格式上有区别，我将其设计为**《世界设定 + 剧情大纲 + 精选场次剧本》**的综合形式。

这份材料既可以直接作为长篇小说的构思蓝本，也可以直接改编为动画、网剧或电影的剧本底稿。

# 项目名称：《剑断苍穹》 (Sword Cuts the Firmament)

## 一、核心概述 (Logline)
在一个修仙者依靠吞噬“众生愿力”而飞升的世界，少年莫离因身负能够看破谎言的“真眼”，被卷入针对天道伪神的阴谋中，他手持无锋锈剑，要在众神崩塌之际，重定人界法则。

## 二、世界观设定 (World Building)

### 1. 境界体系 (修真等级)
1.  **聚气境 (Qi Gathering):** 感应天地灵气。
2.  **筑基境 (Foundation Forging):** 凝聚灵力金丹，脱胎换骨。
3.  **金丹境 (Golden Core):** 寿元两百载，可御剑飞行。
4.  **元婴境 (Nascent Soul):** 灵魂化婴，滴血重生。
5.  **渡劫境 (Calamity Crossing):** 引九天雷劫，冲击飞升。
6.  **真仙境 (True Immortal):** （传说级）飞升上界，成为仙界尊主（实则可能是狱卒）。

### 2. 力量本质
*   **灵气：** 世界的能量源，过度使用会枯竭。
*   **功德/愿力：** 传统修士认为这是飞升之源。
*   **真相：** “飞升通道”实则是通往更高维度的囚笼。所谓的飞升，是将地球的生命精华输送给上界存在的燃料。
*   **莫离的特殊能力：** 【鉴真】。他能看见万物背后的“气数”和虚假的能量流动。

### 3. 地理结构
*   **下界（苍澜大陆）：** 凡人为主，有九大宗门。
*   **浮空岛（天穹城）：** 金丹以上的居所，悬于天际。
*   **断界峡谷：** 通往上界的入口，已被封锁千年。

---

## 三、主要人物小传 (Character Profiles)

| 姓名 | 定位 | 性格特征 | 能力/武器 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **莫离** | 主角 | 隐忍、理智、杀伐果断，内心渴望平静但被迫战斗。 | **残剑·无名：** 无灵光，不吸力，越打越强。拥有【鉴真】瞳术。 |
| **沈清秋** | 女主 | 清冷医修，心怀慈悲，背负家族秘密。 | **银针阵：** 以毒攻毒，治疗兼封印。 |
| **赵无极** | 反派 | 魔道巨擘，坚信弱肉强食，追求力量本身。 | **血煞刀：** 极凶残，吞噬生灵生机。 |
| **天道使者 (王)** | 最终 BOSS | 伪装成守护者的存在，冷漠无情，视众生为蝼蚁。 | **天律锁链：** 锁定因果，禁锢自由。 |

---

## 四、剧情分集大纲 (Story Outline)

### 第一卷：潜龙勿用 (1-20 章/集)
*   **开篇：** 莫离在市井中为一块碎玉所伤，发现能看清玉器内隐藏的杀机。
*   **激励事件：** 宗门大比，天才少年叶飞试图暗杀同门，被莫离当众识破并击败，名声大噪但也招致嫉妒。
*   **试炼：** 参加“青阳秘境”，进入后发现秘境中的妖兽全是人为投放的傀儡，用于筛选有潜力的“飞升祭品”。

### 第二卷：风云激荡 (21-40 章/集)
*   **危机：** 莫离觉醒身体内的异宝“镇狱钉”，引来正道盟追杀。
*   **成长：** 结识女主沈清秋，两人逃亡途中探索上古遗迹。发现“修仙”其实是上界筛选兵种的实验。
*   **高潮：** 决战青阳宗，莫离自断一指激发潜力，将一名元婴长老逼退至虚空裂缝。

### 第三卷：破碎虚空 (41-60 章/集)
*   **揭秘：** 到达浮空岛，得知飞升者皆被“天牢”炼化。
*   **反击：** 组建反抗军“破妄阁”，收集被掠夺的气运。
*   **结局：** 莫离斩断飞升通道，拒绝成为新的“神王”，选择留在人间守护苍生，开启真正的“人道仙途”。

## 五、精选场次剧本 (Selected Script Scenes)

以下提供两个场景的详细剧本格式，展示视觉张力与对话节奏。

### 场次 A：初露锋芒
**背景：** 青云宗 · 演武台。午后。烈日当空，观众席坐满了低阶弟子。
**人物：** 莫离（19 岁）、叶飞（19 岁）、执事长老。

> **【SCENE START】**

> **EXT. 青云宗演武台 - 日**

> 热浪扭曲了空气。台下几百名弟子屏息凝神，目光如炬。

> 莫离站在擂台中央，身穿粗布麻衣，双手抱胸，神情淡漠。他的对面，身着华服的金冠青年叶飞正盘膝而立，周身隐隐泛起金芒。

> **叶飞**
> （嘴角微扬，声音穿透全场）
> 莫师弟，你手中的“废铁”能抵我这一击吗？

> 莫离没有抬头，甚至没有拿剑。他只是轻轻抬起右手，食指和中指并拢。

> **莫离**
> （平静地）
> 师父说，剑未在手，心已在鞘。你太吵了。

> **叶飞**
> （嗤笑）
> 狂！既然你想死，那就让你见识一下——凝气九重！

> **叶飞**

> （轻声自语）
> 破绽太大。

> **MOUJIU**

> 莫离动了。他没有后退，而是向前踏出一步。

> **叶飞**
> （惊呼）

> 就在千钧一发之际，莫离的指尖点在了自己的胸口。

> 叶飞的拳头砸空的瞬间，莫离那把看似生锈的短剑已出现在了他脖颈前，剑柄抵住了皮肤。

> **叶飞**
> （冷汗直流）
> 这……这怎么可能？

> **莫离**
> （收回剑，淡淡道）
> 师兄想再练一次么？下次记得护住咽喉。

> 镜头缓缓上移，莫离身后的阴影里，无数只眼睛死死盯着他，仿佛看到了未来的尸山血海。

> **【SCENE END】**

---

### 场次 B：真相的代价
**背景：** 地下古殿 · 深处密室。四周墙壁由不知名黑色岩石构成，散发着寒气。
**人物：** 莫离、神秘老人（天道守门人）、沈清秋。

> **【SCENE START】**

> **INT. 地下古殿 - 夜**

> 烛火摇曳，却燃烧得很稳。沈清秋坐在石榻上，手中握着半块破碎的令牌。莫立背对着她，手里擦拭着一把黑乎乎的铁剑。

> 什么理由？

> 不是徒劳。因为你们拥有了“恐惧”。恐惧让神明也会感到威胁。

## 六、创作建议与亮点提炼 (Tips for Development)

1.  **爽点设计 (Hook):**
    *   不要一开始就让主角无敌。前期的“反差”很重要（比如别人认为的剑技垃圾，最后却是唯一能克制怪物的）。
    *   战斗要体现“智斗”而非单纯的数值堆砌。利用环境、地形、敌人心理进行博弈。

2.  **情感内核 (Core Theme):**
    *   除了升级打脸，要探讨**“人与神”的关系**。在绝对的力量面前，凡人是否有尊严？
    *   莫离的成长弧光是从“顺从天命”到“质疑天命”，最后是“重塑天命”。

3.  **视觉化语言 (Visuals):**
    *   如果是拍成电视剧，多注重特效与光影的结合（如剑气化龙、空间撕裂）。

4.  **节奏把控:**
    *   每十章一个小高潮（解决一个谜题或小 Boss）。
    *   每五十章一个大高潮（地图转换或身份揭露）。

It was morning. The sun was up, and it was shining. And the grass was cut quite low, which is bad news for someone who is three inches tall.

My name is not important, though I suppose one could call me Number Seventeen. I am a statue. Porcelain. Painted red. I wear boots that never take water, but do not offer any protection against stones. I am standing on a patch of clover in the front yard of a house that belongs to a man who thinks he is smart because he wears a hat to drive.

I need to move. I must cross the lawn.

There are crows.

Now, in my case, crows are not merely birds. They are hunters. They are the kind of people who stand around waiting for the meat to come to them, and then take it. There were seven of them circling over the fence line. They looked at me with eyes like polished coins.

"Do you want me to kill you?" asked Mr. Crow, whose name I assume was Barnaby because it sounded friendly.

"I am a statue," I told him.

"It does not matter," he said. "We only see statues when they do not move."

It was a terrible philosophy, but Mr. Crow spoke it with conviction. He hopped onto the top rail of the chain-link fence. The fence is a barrier between us and the street. It is also a ramp for the predators.

I turned my head. I cannot turn my body. My head is fixed, but I can swivel my neck. The wind blew through my beard, which is made of wire. It felt like hair. I wondered if it was mine, or if the manufacturer had put a wig on me. It did not matter.

I began to walk. It is difficult to walk when you are ceramic. If you trip, you crack. You become a mess of dust on the earth.

I took two steps forward. Then I stopped.

A crow landed on a blade of grass next to my left foot. It pecked at my sandal. It tasted the clay. It found no blood. It laughed. A dry sound, like a leaf being crushed.

"You are heavy," said another crow.

"Yes," I said.

"Too much weight. Too much red paint. You look like you have something valuable in your pocket."

"What is there?"

"Your dignity."

I knew what I needed to do. I had read a book once, written by a soldier who had seen a bomb dropped on a village. It was called *Catch-22*. But I could not find the logic. I had to rely on luck.

The lawn stretched out before me. Green and flat and vast. It looked like a battlefield where nobody had been killed, except for the worms. The worms were hiding underground, digging holes where they could hide from the rain and from the crows.

I walked across the middle of the lawn.

Mr. Crow flew up to the sky. He shouted, "Look! Look!"

Everyone looked at me. Even the ants, though the ants were mostly invisible.

"He is walking toward the hydrant," said a second crow.

"I saw the hydrant," I said. "It is wet."

"Water is dangerous," said the first crow.

"Is it?"

"It tastes like rust."

I kept walking. My boots slipped on the dew. My knees were stiff. My face was painted. I could not scream.

Suddenly, a bird swooped down. I did not know what species it was, but it was the one with the red beak. It landed on my shoulder. It bit my ear. I could hear the teeth rattle against the pottery. I did not fall. I am heavy.

"Let me go," I whispered.

"You cannot," said the crow. "I am holding you now."

"I have nowhere to go."

"There is the house," it said. "But the window is open."

"I cannot fly."

"Then I will carry you," it said.

"No," I said. "That would break you. And then you would be eaten by the cats."

"Then what?"

"We are all alone."

The crow flew away. It did not touch me. It knew that the cat would be faster than it could climb.

I continued. Now I am tired. I am not used to moving. People think that statues do not move, but they lie. We do everything we can to stay still.

When I reached the hydrant, it was wet. The water dripped into my cap. I looked at my reflection in the puddle. I looked older. My cracks were deeper. The white clay was showing through the blue paint.

"Crow!" I shouted.

"What?"

"Go away!"

"I am leaving now."

He lifted himself up into the air. He flew over the fence. He disappeared into the clouds. The sky is full of clouds. It is filled with things that cannot reach us.

I sat down on the hydrant. I was shaking. It was not cold. It was only that I was afraid.

And then I realized something. The crows would return tomorrow. They would bring friends. They would bring their children. They would come for all of us, even the ones who stay still.

They will take me.

There is no way to stop it. It is not our fault. It is just the way things are. We are here. Then we are gone. The lawn will grow taller. The grass will cover me.

I closed my eyes.

And I waited.

There is no need to worry about whether we survive. There is only the fact that we exist. And that is enough.

It was very hard to tell. But in the end, I guess we all knew.

**Martín:**
—Buenas tardes. Tengo una pregunta. No es una de las usuales del examen.

**Clara:**
—(Sin apartar la vista de las tarjetas) —¿Una sobre los precios? ¿O tal vez pases de seguridad si olvidaste algo en casa? Ya sabes que cierramos en media hora...

**Martín:**
—No es eso. (Se detiene a la mitad del pasillo, apretando la mano detrás de sus pantalones). Hoy cumplí dieciocho años. Por primera vez en diez años... siento que tengo permiso para ser sincero contigo. En serio.

**Clara:**
—(Se da vuelta, sonriendo con cierta tristeza sarcástica) —Sé muy bien qué edad tienes. Y sé que te gusta mi trabajo porque yo siempre tengo galletas o chicles en la caja. Martín, eres inteligente, no creas que no te veo. Pero decirme algo así ahora... es ridículo.

**Martín:**
—¿Es ridículo? ¿Por qué lo dices?

**Clara:**
—(Ajusta la diadema en el cabello) —Eres un adolescente. Yo soy esta mujer cansada que pasa su jornada entera haciendo cuentas y mirando clientes. Tú eres mi cliente regular desde que tenía seis años. ¿Crees que voy a creer que este sentimiento es serio? Piensas que es una broma de cumpleañero.

**Martín:**
—No es una broma. Lo sé. Lo sé muy bien. Cuando tenía siete años vi tu cara en la ventana, cuando tenías doce años guardé silencio cuando te mudaste a otro piso porque sentía que te veía triste. Te vi crecer, señora... pero no pude.

**(Se acerca más a la barra, bajando la cabeza)**

**Martín:**
—Me quedé callado porque tenía miedo. Tenía miedo de parecer un idiota. De que me echaran la puerta en la nariz. Pero hoy, Martina, hoy que soy mayor de edad... quiero que sepas que no me importan tus horarios ni mis notas. Solo me importa que estés aquí.

**Clara:**
—(Su voz se suaviza, pierde el tono distante) —Tienes dieciocho años. Yo tengo tres veces tanto tiempo trabajando, Martín. Vivirás mucho antes de que entiendas la complejidad de esto. No somos lo mismo.

**Martín:**
—Lo sé. Sé que somos diferentes en experiencia, en edad. Pero también sabemos que no hay nada falso en esto. Soy viejo para ser tan joven en sentimientos, quizás. Y tú... tú eres nueva para sentirse vieja.

**Clara:**
—(Calla un momento. Mira el reloj. Suspira.) —No sé qué significa eso que dijiste. Ser nuevo para sentirlo viejo... Es confuso.

**Martín:**
—Quiero decir que te admiraba siempre, pero quería estar cerca. Y hoy ya puedo esperar, sí. Porque no me vas a ver como un niño.

**Clara:**
—(Da un paso atrás. Se queda mirándolo fijamente en los ojos). —Te creo. Pero no por eso cambiará nada de mañana en adelante. Quieres hacer un regalo a mi soledad con palabras bonitas. Y no te culparía. Tienes todo el derecho del mundo a tener esos sueños.

**Martín:**
—No estoy aquí para pedirte que cambies tus horas ni para obligarte. Estaba en la puerta, buscando la forma de decirlo. Si te alejas de mí, entenderé que el amor no es para todos. Pero te prometí que sería honesto. Fue mi única intención.

**Clara:**
—(Asiente lentamente, recogiendo la caja de galletas vacía) —Honestidad. Esa sí. Algo raras veces tenemos. Bienvenido a la edad adulta, Martín. Ojalá seas capaz de mantener esa palabra tan bien.

**Martín:**
—Lo haré. Gracias por escucharme. Aunque sea mentira en principio.

**Clara:**
—(Sonríe levemente, una sonrisa genuina y suave) —Fue solo la verdad. Y no mentí. Te escuche, chico. Y... bueno, no es un mal cumpleaños. Al menos hoy hablaste sin tapujos.

**(Se levanta para cerrar la caja. Él permanece allí, mirándola mientras ella vuelve a ordenar, sintiendo que el aire entre ellos cambió para siempre).**

**TITLE:** TAKAMAKI TITANS

**CHARACTERS:**

**ANN TAKAMAKI (17)** – Bubbly, energetic, perpetually optimistic, secretly loves carbs more than logic. Wears a pink tracksuit when she's exercising.

**JOKER (UNSEEN)** – Only heard at the end.

[SCENE START]

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - LIVING ROOM - DAY**

The living room is pristine but cluttered with gym accessories. A punching bag swings slightly from a wall mount. A yoga mat is rolled out in the center of the carpet.

ANN stands in front of a full-length mirror. She adjusts a bright PINK headband and pulls her hair into a messy ponytail. She is wearing neon green leggings and a white crop top.

She looks determined. Too determined.

<center>ANN</center>
> Okay... Ann... Today is the day! No more "diet." No more hiding under the sweater. We're going to burn those calories before they even land!

She grabs a heavy-looking water bottle and hits the music play button on her phone. Upbeat J-Pop blasts loudly.

**ANN**

She immediately starts doing high knees, jogging in place. Then jumps onto the couch.

Then she pauses. She looks down at her stomach. It doesn't move much.

<center>ANN</center>
> Hmph. Still too flat...

She takes off the headband. She sits heavily on the floor. Her face goes from heroic determination to mild sadness.

<center>ANN</center>
> (Muttering)
> Just one crunch... if I don't do it, my thighs might grow.

She leans forward. She sees her reflection. She pats her own thigh gently.

<center>ANN</center>
> Oh no. They feel so heavy today. Like rocks! Or chocolate bars!

She sighs. Her resolve evaporates. She stands up, stretches, and heads toward the kitchenette.

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - KITCHENETTE - CONTINUOUS**

Ann opens a cabinet door. It squeaks loudly.

Inside is NOT cereal. Inside are SNACKS.

There is a massive bag of GUMMI BEARS. There is a tub of ICE CREAM labeled "BINGO". There is half a loaf of bread.

<center>ANN</center>
> (Whispering)
> Hey, little guy. You look so... lonely.

She pulls out the GUMMI BEAR bag. Snaps it open with enthusiasm.

<center>ANN</center>
> Hehe! Exercise is great for my heart, but food is great for my soul! And honestly, right now, my soul is feeling a little hungry.

She pops three gummies into her mouth at once. Chews them rapidly.

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - LIVING ROOM - MOMENTS LATER**

Ann is now lying on the yoga mat. She looks defeated.

<center>ANN</center>
> My legs... they won't listen anymore. If I run, they're going to cry.

She sits up. She opens the second cabinet drawer.

**CLOSE UP:**
A large, glass bowl filled with fruit slices. Next to it, a tub of strawberry yogurt.

Ann pushes the fruit aside with a gloved hand.

<center>ANN</center>
> No, fruits are healthy... but strawberries taste like hugs. And hugs should always be sweetened.

She grabs two strawberries. Then drops the spoon.

She opens the fridge.

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - Fridge SHOT**

Shelves of convenience store meals. Ramen cups. Bento boxes. A jar of pickles. A single box of pudding that is empty except for condensation.

Ann reaches for the last one.

<center>ANN</center>
> (Horrified excitement)
> Aha! The final pudding! That was for... for lunch!

She opens the lid. Smells it deeply. Her eyes widen.

<center>ANN</center>
> It smells like victory.

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - KITCHEN - ONE HOUR LATER**

A montage sequence set to upbeat, distorted jazz music.

*   Ann eats a whole slice of cake while balancing it with chopsticks.
*   She pours milk over crackers.
*   She holds a soda can up like a potion bottle. "For stamina."
*   She wipes her mouth and licks the frosting off the spatula.
*   She sits on the counter in pajamas, legs splayed, covered in crumbs.

**INT. TAKAMAKI HOME - LIVING ROOM - EVENING**

The sun is setting outside the window. Dust motes dance in the light.

Ann lies on her back on the yoga mat. She looks exhausted. She has crumbs scattered across her chest. A crumb is lodged in her eyebrow.

She sighs, looking up at the ceiling fan.

<center>ANN</center>
> My body... it was so heavy before I started running. But now? Now it's... soft. And fluffy. Like cloud armor!

She closes her eyes, smiling blissfully.

<center>ANN</center>
> Tomorrow... I'll try the squat routine again! Maybe next week I'll buy the protein shake.

She turns her head slowly to the side. A knock at the door.

Ann freezes. She scrambles to wipe crumbs off her face with the corner of a napkin.

<center>ANN</center>
> Shh! Quiet! Don't announce me yet!

She peeks through the crack in the curtain.

**THE DOOR OPENS.**

It's not Joker yet. Just a delivery man.

<center>DELIVERY MAN</center>
> Delivery for the Takamaki residence.

Ann slams the door shut. She rushes to the kitchen to grab a cookie and offers it as a peace offering.

<center>ANN</center>
> Just kidding! We weren't doing anything weird! Nothing happened!

**THE DOOR OPENS AGAIN.**

This time, JOKER walks in. He's holding a takeout bag.

Joker stops. He tilts his head.

<center>JOKER</center>
> Did you... order a bento? Or are you cooking? The smell coming from the hallway is pretty strong.

Ann covers her nose dramatically.

<center>ANN</center>
> Ahem! Oh, it's just... umm... air! Fresh air! Well, stale air mixed with cinnamon! From the oven!

Joker steps closer. He raises an eyebrow. He looks at the pile of trash bags near the sink. One is already overflowing.

<center>JOKER</center>
> That wasn't fresh air, Ann. That was a sugar bomb.

<center>ANN</center>
> (Defensive)
> What?! Who told you?! You shouldn't be reading into things! I was just... preparing a light snack! For strength building! To protect myself from bad vibes!

She hops off the mat, waving her hands.

<center>ANN</center>
> See? This is why we need you, Joker! You bring snacks every week. You know how it is! We share!

She runs to him and shoves a handful of jelly beans into his hand.

<center>ANN</center>
> Here. Take a bite. Taste the effort!

Joker takes a bite. He closes his eyes. Nods approvingly.

<center>JOKER</center>
> Mmm. It's good. Very sweet. Very... you.

<center>ANN</center>
> (Beaming)
> Right? You understand us! So, since you liked it... you'll help clean up the mess after dinner? Please?

Joker looks at the mess. Looks at Ann. Looks at the camera. He sighs, but smiles.

<center>JOKER</center>
> Only if you stop calling it "light snacks."

<center>ANN</center>
> Deal. But I'm calling it "fuel."

**FADE OUT.**

**TEXT ON SCREEN:**
"Diet plans start tomorrow... or yesterday? Sometimes, the answer doesn't matter."

[END OF SCRIPT]

Here are the step-by-step solutions to the thermodynamic problem.

### **Assumptions and Property Data**
We utilize standard steam table data (based on IAPWS-97 or similar textbook standards like Cengel & Boles).
*   **State 1 (Inlet Water):** $P_1 = 1.0 \text{ bar}$, $T_1 = 20^\circ\text{C}$.
    *   Substance is a compressed liquid. We approximate using saturated liquid properties at $20^\circ\text{C}$.
    *   $h_1 \approx h_f @ 20^\circ\text{C} = 83.91 \text{ kJ/kg}$
    *   $s_1 \approx s_f @ 20^\circ\text{C} = 0.2965 \text{ kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}$
*   **State 3 (High Pressure Steam):** $P_3 = 10 \text{ bar}$, $T_3 = 400^\circ\text{C}$.
    *   $h_3 = 3263.9 \text{ kJ/kg}$
    *   $s_3 = 7.4651 \text{ kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}$
*   **State 4s (Isentropic Turbine Exit):** $P_4 = 1.0 \text{ bar}$, $s_{4s} = s_3 = 7.4651 \text{ kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}$.
    *   At 1.0 bar, saturated vapor entropy $s_g = 7.3594 \text{ kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}$.
    *   Since $s_{4s} > s_g$, the state is **Superheated**.
    *   Interpolating Steam Tables at 1.0 bar for $s = 7.4651$:
        *   Between $150^\circ\text{C}$ ($s=7.6134, h=2776.4$) and $100^\circ\text{C}$ ($s=7.3594, h=2675.5$).
        *   Calculated Isentropic Enthalpy $h_{4s} = 2717.4 \text{ kJ/kg}$.

---

### **a.) Rate at which heat must be supplied**

We apply the First Law of Thermodynamics to the Heat Exchanger (energy balance on the water stream).
$$ \dot{Q}_{in} = \dot{m}_w (h_3 - h_2) $$

First, determine $h_2$ from the Pump Energy Balance:
$$ \dot{W}_{pump} = \dot{m}_w (h_2 - h_1) \implies h_2 = h_1 + \frac{\dot{W}_{pump}}{\dot{m}_w} $$
$$ h_2 = 83.91 + \frac{110}{45} = 83.91 + 2.44 = 86.35 \text{ kJ/kg} $$

Now calculate $\dot{Q}_{in}$:
$$ \dot{Q}_{in} = 45 \text{ kg/s} \times (3263.9 - 86.35) \text{ kJ/kg} $$
$$ \dot{Q}_{in} = 45 \times 3177.55 = 142,990 \text{ kW} $$

**Answer:** The rate of heat supplied is approximately **143 MW** (or 143,000 kW).

---

### **b.) Power produced by the turbine**

We use the definition of Turbine Isentropic Efficiency:
$$ \eta_T = \frac{\dot{W}_{turb, act}}{\dot{W}_{turb, isen}} = \frac{\dot{m}_w (h_3 - h_4)}{\dot{m}_w (h_3 - h_{4s})} $$

Calculate Isentropic Work per unit mass:
$$ w_{t, isen} = h_3 - h_{4s} = 3263.9 - 2717.4 = 546.5 \text{ kJ/kg} $$

Calculate Actual Work per unit mass:
$$ w_{t, act} = 0.71 \times 546.5 = 388.0 \text{ kJ/kg} $$

Calculate Total Turbine Power:
$$ \dot{W}_{turb} = \dot{m}_w \times w_{t, act} $$
$$ \dot{W}_{turb} = 45 \text{ kg/s} \times 388.0 \text{ kJ/kg} = 17,460 \text{ kW} $$

**Answer:** The power produced by the turbine is approximately **17.5 MW** (or 17,460 kW).

---

### **c.) Total rate of entropy production**

The total entropy production for the system is calculated by summing the entropy changes of the exiting and entering streams within the control volume (Water and Exhaust Gases).
$$ \dot{S}_{gen} = \dot{S}_{system\_change} + \sum \frac{\dot{Q}}{T_{boundary}} $$
Since the outer boundary is assumed adiabatic (only heat exchange is internal between streams), $\dot{Q}_{boundary} = 0$.

***

Внутри бетонной камеры царит непроницаемая тьма, разорванная лишь тусклым синим свечением мониторов на панели управления и факелом от генератора холодного света, рассеивающего пыльцу на стенах из армированного бетона C50. Стены покрыты анти-статическим слоем, а пол представляет собой плиту из сверхпрочного композита с встроенными электромагнитными демпферами. Воздух здесь имеет специфический химический запах: озоновый шлейф, смешанный с металлической коррозией и холодным азотом систем охлаждения криостатов.

Камера находится под круглосуточным наблюдением.
На посту охраны стоит ЧИНОНОСИТЕЛЬ ОТДЕЛА ОХРАНЫ №428, его лицо скрыто стандартным противогазом класса A. Он держит в руках пистолет системы МР-78, заряженный патронами .50 кал., но не стучится, просто стоит в жесткой позе. Рядом с ним стоит второй охранник, который уже тридцать минут чистил оптику своей винтовки. Они тихо переговариваются, обсуждая усталость и новую норму часовых обменов, пока невидимо для камеры система видеонаблюдения сканирует их лица на предмет подозрительной активности.

На теле закреплены несколько тонких светящихся кабелей — нейроинтерфейсов для считывания данных мозговой активности и предотвращения неконтролируемых выбросов энергии. # The Age of the Triad: The World 20 Years After

**Date:** November 14, 2044  
**Location:** Global Overview  
**Theme:** *Perception as Reality, Order through Rewind, Chaos as Spectacle*

Twenty years after the convergence of their desires, the world exists in a paradoxical state. Humanity has reached a level of cultural perfection unimagined in any prior century, yet beneath the gilded surface lies a civilization fractured by the interplay of absolute time control, absolute fame, and absolute charisma.

### I. The Atmosphere: A Stagnant Perfection
The year is marked by a phenomenon called **"The Serenity Loop."** For three decades, humanity has been unable to experience a truly negative global event. Wars were halted before escalation. Economic crashes were reversed into booms within minutes. This occurred not because humanity learned peace, but because one woman rewound reality every time disaster threatened the status quo.

However, the result is not utopia. Because history loops back to the last moment where the outcome was optimal, human innovation has stalled. Every failure is erased before it teaches a lesson. Art, science, and industry rely on repetition of the same successful patterns, curated by the perceptions of the most influential women alive.

### II. Character Portraits

#### 1. Seraphina "Sera" Moreau (Age 80) – *The Architect*
**Status:** *Living Legend / Hidden Sovereign*

Sera is now an octogenarian who physically resembles a ghost haunting the edges of history. She never steps into the public eye. Her high **Judgement (10)** prevents her from making emotional mistakes, while her **Low Social Good (2)** ensures she does not use her power for altruism. She uses her time manipulation solely to curate her own narrative and maximize the longevity of her wealth and legacy.

*   **Life:** She lives in a climate-controlled estate in New Zealand, isolated. She possesses multiple identities across history—some are fictionalized memoirs, others are erased timelines.
*   **The Burden:** Sera has noticed that the timeline is fracturing due to the presence of Lena and Elara. Their chaotic energies threaten to destabilize the very fabric of cause-and-effect she relies on.
*   **Role:** She is the "Director" of the timeline. When Lena makes a risky move that threatens global safety, Sera pauses time, reverts to the hour before, and adjusts the variables slightly to prevent catastrophe without changing the outcome. She essentially acts as a fail-safe system for the world, though she views humans merely as assets or liabilities in her equation.

#### 2. Lena Delgado (Age 39) – *The Muse*
**Status:** *Global Thought Leader / Cultural Symbol*

Originally a teenager seeking validation, Lena has blossomed into the definition of "Genius" in the collective consciousness. Her wish granted her universal belief in her talent. She does not need to code software to build systems; she commands developers to write perfect code. She does not need to paint to create masterpieces; critics weep at her sketches that were doodles in a sketchbook.

*   **Impact:** She holds more influence than any head of state. Nations sign treaties because her Wit (9) makes her words sound like wisdom. Her **Hedonism (8)** means she spends her wealth lavishly, funding mega-projects designed for entertainment rather than utility.
*   **Relationship with Power:** She is the first woman elected as a non-partisan Chancellor of a coalition of nations. Not because she was chosen, but because everyone assumes she would be the best choice possible.
*   **Weakness:** Her **Low Knowledge (3)** has made her dependent on a massive intelligence network maintained by Elara and Sera. She knows how things look, but not always how they work.

#### 3. Elara Oakwood (Age 42) – *The Idol*
**Status:** *The Face of Planet Earth*

Elara’s wish created the ultimate influencer. She is undeniably beautiful, charming, and radiant. She possesses a magnetic aura that compels strangers to help, lovers to forgive, and enemies to surrender. However, her **Low Judgement (2)** makes her reckless. She often ignores consequences until the moment she realizes a problem is happening, at which point she runs away or is saved.

*   **Life:** She travels the globe in luxury. She owns islands. She wears clothes woven from rare materials. Yet, she remains perpetually single, despite the fact that her **Charisma (8)** usually results in millions of suitors. The men who pursue her are often discarded quickly because she simply perceives them as "boring" for the day, which they accept gracefully.
*   **Economy:** She monetizes her attention. She can walk into a factory and double production because everyone works harder to please her gaze. She is also the face of "Beauty Standards"; if she sneezes blue, half the world's makeup industry shifts color.

---

### III. Dynamics & Interactions: The Triangle of Influence

Over the past two decades, these three have developed a symbiotic relationship that defines the era.

**1. Sera vs. The Others (Control)**
Sera is the only person who sees the "truth." While Lena and Elara manipulate perception and social trends, Sera manipulates physics. However, she dislikes the interference.
*   **Conflict:** In 2025, Elara was involved in a diplomatic spat that could have triggered a war. Sera rewound the meeting, stopping the conflict. Elara saw nothing wrong with the conversation initially, assuming she was persuasive enough. Only after Sera showed her the recording did she realize the magic intervened.
*   **Tension:** Sera refuses to allow Elara or Lena to change their behavior permanently. "Change the timeline, not the people," she dictates. She forces the world to reset repeatedly until they make the "right" decision.

**2. Lena vs. Elara (Perception War)**
Though both seek adoration, their styles differ. Lena is the Mind; Elara is the Body.
*   **Rivalry:** They compete for titles. Media outlets are split: "Delgado Intelligence" vs. "Oakwood Entertainment."
*   **Cooperation:** They rely on each other's strengths. Elara provides the charisma to rally populations; Lena provides the intellectual justification for policies. Together, they form a tripartite government structure known as the "Triumvirate."
*   **Jealousy:** There is underlying tension regarding time. Elara has noticed that Lena ages slower mentally and socially. Lena suspects Elara is hiding something. Neither dares confront the other directly because their interaction triggers a mutual adrenaline spike that sustains their popularity.

**3. The "Grandchildren" Void**
A critical aspect of the world 20 years later is its demographics. All three characters remain childless.
*   **Sera:** Her lack of **Family Priority (5)** meant she focused entirely on her own survival and reputation. She has used time magic to prevent the death of her late spouse multiple times, creating a life of eternal widowhood where she is never quite settled in grief.
*   **Lena & Elara:** Their high **Hedonism** and focus on external validation left little room for domestic commitment. Lena's relationships are viewed as professional collaborations by the public. Elara's relationships are treated as fleeting inspirations by the media.
*   **Societal Impact:** With few people having children, the population is stabilizing around this core demographic. Children are raised exclusively to study under the Triumvirate’s tutelage. They worship the three women as the architects of modern existence.

---

### IV. The World State 20 Years Later

**Culture:**
Art is homogenous. Since Lena's talent guarantees success, artists only copy styles she approves of. Music follows rhythms Elara finds pleasant. Innovation is discouraged because Sera rewinds any project that fails to replicate the initial success rate.

## PRODUCTION DOCUMENTMENT & EPISODE BREAKDOWN

**Series:** Star Trek: The Next Generation

### LOGLINE
A strange, non-corporeal frequency emitted from the Bassenberg Nebula begins to alter the neural patterns of the crew. As Captain Picard races to decode the origin of the signal, he discovers the signal contains the exact memories of the people it touches—erased from their minds and rewritten by a dormant, pre-warp artifact trapped within the nebula.

- **James T. Kirk/Jonathan Archer:** No involvement.
- **J.J./Hendrix:** No involvement.
- **William Riker:** Active Commanding Officer of the Red Alert Bridge Team.

### PART 1 BREAKDOWN: "THE RESONANCE"

#### SCENE 1: OPENING SEQUENCE (STANDARD)
*(Visuals: Deep space, nebula, starfield. Music: Main Theme. Text fades in: "STAR TREK: THE NEXT GENERATION")*

#### SCENE 2: ENTERPRISE-D BRIDGE – DAY
**LOG ENTRY**
Captain Picard stands before the viewscreen.
"The Enterprise-D is investigating a localized anomaly near coordinates 0-9-4-X."

Riker sits at the tactical console. Data stands beside Picard. Troi stands in the science station. Worf is reviewing sensor logs on the center screen.

<center>RIKER</center>
> Sensors read zero mass density there, Captain.

<center>PICARD</center>
> And yet, your instruments report a persistent signal pulse repeating every 74 seconds.

<center>DATA</center>
> Correct. The signal emits a frequency that does not propagate through conventional electromagnetic waves. It bypasses sensors entirely and registers directly as... neural activity in my cranial processors.

<center>PICARD</center>
> What is its source, Data?

<center>DATA</center>
> Unknown. There is no object generating the signal. The energy originates from the void itself.

<center>WORF</center>
> Ma'am. I detect residual interference in the lower decks. The mess hall ventilation fans are running cold despite the atmospheric temperature. Crew personnel have reported hearing humming.

**ACTION:** Picard turns his gaze to the helm.
<center>PICARD</center>
> Mr. Crusher. Do you have any medical readings on your crew?
<center>CROUSEL (OFFSCREEN)</center>
> *[Voice on Comms]* Negative, Captain. But Dr. Troi reports... unusual lucidity levels. Several crew members claim they've "remembered" things they couldn't possibly know.

#### SCENE 3: MEDICAL BAY – CONTINUOUS
Beverly Crusher examines a patient. Dr. Troi stands nearby.

<center>CRUSHER</center>
> You're certain? This isn't fatigue?

<center>TROI</center>
> Not exactly fatigue. These individuals—Mr. Worf, Mr. La Forge, Ensign Sisko—they claim they were once in a different timeline, Commander. They recall seeing the nebula before we arrived. But the data shows they haven't been near the nebula yet.

<center>CRUSHER</center>
> Time travel? Temporal displacement?

<center>TROI</center>
> I'm not saying it's possible. I'm saying it's happening in their neural pathways. It's like someone put a recording inside their head and told them it was their own.

#### SCENE 4: BRIDGE – LATER THAT NIGHT
Picard is seated, arms crossed. Riker reports from his desk.

<center>RIKER</center>
> We tried scanning the nebula with the warp core drive active. Nothing changed. Even with the engines, the pulse keeps hitting us.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Can we isolate the source?

<center>Riker</center>
> The sensors lock onto the crew, sir. It's like the signal is targeting us specifically.

<center>Data</center>
> Hypothesis: We are receiving the signal, not because it finds us. But because we are compatible with it. The organism generating it requires a biological carrier to function.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Data, shut down the impulse drives. Move back to safe distance.

#### SCENE 5: SCIENCE STATION – NEXT MORNING
Picard reviews a holographic projection. Data stands by.

<center>DATA</center>
> Analysis confirms the waveform matches a pattern of biological memory storage. Specifically, human memory patterns encoded in a crystalline lattice structure.

<center>PICARD</center>
> You believe this is an artificial construct?

<center>DATA</center>
> Likely. However, the complexity defies current understanding. It is not merely transmitting information; it is altering the observer's state of consciousness.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Who designed such a device? And why now?

<center>DATA</center>
> The signal has been silent for three centuries. It began repeating approximately twenty minutes ago.

<center>PICARD</center>
> That coincides with our approach to the outer rim.

<center>DATA</center>
> Precisely. Something woke it up.

#### SCENE 6: LOWER DECKS – CORRIDOR
Worf walks through the corridor. A security guard stops him.

<center>GUARD</center>
> Lieutenant Worf? Are you alright? You looked like you'd seen a ghost.

<center>WORF</center>
> I have not seen ghosts. But I do remember being here. Before today.

**VISUAL EFFECT:** The scene freezes slightly. A red hue washes over the corridor walls briefly before returning to normal. Worf stares blankly.

<center>WORF</center>
> *[Internal monologue]* My father... my mother... they died in 2380. But in the memory, they are alive. Yet I cannot access the visual data. Only the feeling.

<center>GUARD</center>
> I'll get MedBay on line for you.

<center>WORF</center>
> I don't need a doctor. I need answers.

#### SCENE 7: BRIDGE – FINAL MOMENT
Troi enters the bridge. She looks unsettled. She speaks directly into her communicator.

<center>TROI</center>
> Captain Picard?

<center>PICARD</center>
> Deanna? Report.

<center>TROI</center>
> It's getting worse. I'm sensing a presence. Not inside me. Outside. Something is calling us. And it wants us to listen.

**CUT TO:** Picard turns to the viewscreen. A faint light flickers on the glass—a reflection that wasn't there before.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Mr. Data. Run a diagnostic on the entire ship. Every system. Every person. I want a full audit by lightspeed.

<center>DATA</center>
> Understood.

**CUT TO:**
**EXT. ENTIRE SYSTEM – SHOT OF NEBULA**
The nebula pulses with a golden light. Inside the clouds, a silhouette glimmers faintly. A shapeless form made of shifting particles.

<center>DATA (OVERCOM)</center>
> Source confirmed. It is not emanating from the nebula. It is emerging from the dark matter cloud itself.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Hold position. Do not transmit.

<center>RIKER</center>
> Sir, if it's a lifeform, we could be walking into a trap.

<center>PICARD</center>
> Or we could be the first to speak in thousands of years. Mr. La Forge, prep the transporters. I want to sample the air. Just a few puffs of atmosphere from the surface.

<center>LA FORGE</center>
> Sir? That's not safe protocol.

<center>PICARD</center>
> And the protocol is failing. Prepare for deployment.

**FADE OUT.**

---

### PART 1 KEY DIALOGUE MONTAGE (FOR REFERENCE)

**PICARD:**
"I find that when you look at the stars, you see something beyond the immediate horizon. You see a possibility."

**DATA:**
"A possibility I cannot calculate, Captain. I have no answer for the unknown. I simply observe it."

**TROCI:**
"It's the fear, Jean-Luc. Not of death. Of forgetting. If we forget who we are, we are nothing."

**RIKER:**
"I've never felt a ship shake like this. Not even near the Klingon border. This is different. This is quiet."

---

### PRODUCTION NOTES FOR PARTS 2-5 (SUMMARY)
*To maintain continuity for future episodes:*
1.  **Part 2:** Introduce the "Entity." The nebula reveals its true nature.

**Working Title:** *The Long Silence*

In the brooding atmosphere of the American West, grief is not a sharp blow; it is the slow erosion of the stone. Following the tragic loss of Jack Twist, Ennis Del Mar must navigate a landscape that demands he forget, even as the mountains demand he remember. Here are ten short story concepts exploring Ennis’s solitary journey after his lover is gone.

### 1. The Last Nail
Ennis arrives at a hardware store in small-town Wyoming to buy a single nail—a rusted, bent piece of scrap metal he finds in his pocket. He intends to give it to the undertaker to attach to Jack's casket. At the counter, he meets a mechanic named Sam who recognizes the shape of the scrap. It's a specific type used only in the 1962 model year of a specific truck. When Ennis explains why he needs it, Sam reveals he once repaired Ennis' own truck. The story ends with Ennis buying the truck parts he thinks he needs to repair the casket, realizing the weight of carrying Jack's memory rests not in objects, but in the maintenance of a life that is slowly breaking down around him.

### 2. The Unburned Photo
Years later, while cleaning out an attic inherited from a distant cousin, Ennis finds a photograph tucked inside the lining of his coat. It’s one he thought he threw away years ago—the shot of them standing on the ridge line, wind whipping the hair off their faces. The image is scratched, the bottom corner torn. As Ennis runs a thumb over the damage, he realizes the tears came from him, not the washing machine. He spends the night folding the corners perfectly with a ruler, refusing to cut it out, deciding that if the image is damaged, it remains part of the truth of what happened, rather than pretending it didn't happen.

### 3. Hell Creek, November
Ennis returns to his wife Alma's parents in Hell Creek for a visit. The house smells like stale tobacco and boiled vegetables. While sitting in the kitchen, he overhears Alma discussing her mother-in-law's illness with the cousins. She mentions a plan to sell the family land, saying, "If she goes, we move on." Ennis freezes. He looks at Alma, sees the fear in her eyes, and quietly hands her a receipt for groceries he bought earlier. He doesn't say a word. He leaves. The story focuses on the silence between them; he knows he cannot leave with her because she will not understand the silence of his grief, and he cannot stay because the silence here is too loud.

### 4. The Boy's Name
A young woman shows up at Ennis' cabin, asking for directions to the Bighorn Peak campground. She holds a sketchbook filled with drawings of horses. She claims she is a relative of a girl who lived there twenty years ago. Ennis listens politely but tells her he doesn't know her name. When the sun sets and the shadows stretch across the floorboards, she leaves a note under the door. It reads: "Your friend Jack said you would know me." Ennis opens it, reads it, and walks outside to look at the sky. It is the first time he acknowledges aloud that he remembers Jack.

### 5. The Winter Cattle Drive
During a harsh winter storm, Ennis is forced to drive a herd of cows across a frozen lake. A calf slips on the ice and tumbles into the water. Instinctively, Ennis jumps in, dragging the animal to shore, though he risks his own safety. Later, drying off, he pulls up the blanket where he slept. Underneath lies a piece of red velvet Jack left behind from a dress. The warmth of the fire makes him realize that his survival now depends on the same instinct that saved him when they were young. He wraps the velvet around the calf and carries it into the barn.

### 6. The Engine That Roars
Ennis drives to a scrapyard to sell the old Chevy pickup he has owned since the war. It’s not just his car; it’s the one he drove with Jack all over the state. The mechanic asks, "What did you do with it?" Ennis says nothing. He watches the car get crushed. As the jaws close, he hears the crunch of metal, which sounds almost like breathing. He walks away before the car is fully flattened, leaving the engine intact so it can run again one day. He promises the scrapyard worker, "It’ll run again," knowing he means it as a promise to himself.

### 7. The Church Bell
Ennis attends a church service in town. The congregation sings a hymn. The bell rings loudly, startling him. He stands up to leave but stops. A neighbor whispers, "We have a guest. From out of state." Ennis knows it’s Jack’s brother. Ennis sits in the back row, watching the brother speak to the pastor about building a community center. The brother looks directly at him. There is a question in the air. Ennis nods once. It is a silent acknowledgment that this is not a community they built, but one they survived.

### 8. The Letter in the Box
Ennis sorts through Jack's belongings. In a wooden box, he finds a collection of letters written by Jack to their children (who never met). He reads them by candlelight. They talk about hope, about the future. He pauses on a letter dated two days before the accident, where Jack writes, "You are my strength." He closes the book. He knows he doesn't want to show Alma the letter. He keeps it hidden. It belongs to him. It is the only thing he owns that isn't a burden.

### 9. The Train Journey
Taking a train ride to the nearest city where there might be a doctor, Ennis finds a seat next to a woman who smells of lavender. They discuss travel. "Where to?" she asks. "To see you," he replies. She laughs. He corrects her. "No. To leave. To see where you went when you stopped." She stares at him. She understands. He tells her about the man waiting for him, even though he is dead. She nods. "I know," she says. The train whistle blows, and he realizes he does not wish to arrive at the station yet. He wants to stay on the train.

### 10. The Final Morning
Ennis wakes early, before dawn. He puts on his boots, but before lacing them, he pauses. He places them side by side. He remembers when they stood at the foot of the mountain and watched the sun come up together. He dresses in his work clothes, grabs his rifle. He walks out to the fields. He doesn't shoot anything. He just listens to the wind through the corn. He realizes that Jack is still in the wind. He walks back inside and turns off the light. The room is dark, and Ennis Del Mar is finally at peace.

Here is a character profile designed to be emotionally complex, visually striking, and functionally vital to your story.

### **Character Profile: Eris Vance**
**(Nickname: "The Hollow")**

**Visual Appearance:**
*   **Face:** Heart-stoppingly beautiful with skin like porcelain. Her most striking feature is her eyes—hollow rings of silver-paint around irises that shift color based on her mood (gold when arrogant, red when desperate, black when hunting). She wears her eyeliner thick and dark, almost like kohl, which she claims helps her "hide the light that follows her."
*   **Hair:** Platinum blonde, cut into a jagged bob that falls just below her jawline. She always keeps two strands hanging loosely over her face.
*   **Attire:** She rejects armor. She wears a customized high-fashion trench coat made of matte-black leather and a fabric that seems to absorb light. Underneath is a white silk bodysuit and fishnets. On her feet are gravity-defying boots. She carries no heavy weapons; she fights bare-handed using her ability.
*   **Signature Accessory:** A large, ornate ring on her left hand that contains a void-like gemstone. This is the "Key" she uses to execute her abilities.

**Role:** The Special Mission's Primary Scout & "Asset Manager" (Protagonist Partner).
**Special Skill:** *"Conceptual Larceny"* (The Absolute Theft).

***

**The Ability: Conceptual Larceny**
Eris does not simply break open safes or scale walls. She has the ability to **strip concepts** from reality.
*   **Locks/Barriers:** She doesn't unlock them; she steals the *function* of the mechanism. A laser grid stops working not because she disabled it, but because she stole the "logic" of its activation.
*   **Guardians/Sentinels:** She can temporarily steal an enemy's "aggression" or "reflexes." An invincible knight might suddenly freeze in confusion as Eris steals the concept of "Combat Readiness."
*   **Ultimate Move:** She can attempt to steal **Value**. If she grabs a priceless diamond, she can turn it into a rock for everyone else while keeping the diamond's *appearance*, selling it for infinite profit.
*   **The Catch:** The Gods did not choose her to be a hero. They chose her because she is the only one who knows how to steal **Destiny**.

**Non-Standard Personality:**
Eris is not the "cute delinquent" archetype. She is colder, more cynical, and manipulative. She treats the mission like a transaction and the people on it like variables.
*   **Public Persona:** Charming, witty, and terrifyingly confident. She smiles even when facing death. She is known to flirt with danger rather than avoid it.
*   **Private Reality:** Eris suffers from **Emotional Amnesia**. Every time she uses a high-level theft of a "concept" or "memory" on someone else, she accidentally deletes a piece of her own history. She doesn't know exactly who her parents are anymore. She is beautiful, but she fears mirrors because she worries she doesn't recognize herself in them.
*   **The Negative Trait:** She is addicted to the *feeling* of control. She hates being protected. When the MC tries to save her, she panics and runs away. She views trust as "weakness that makes you vulnerable to having your memories stolen."

**Weaponry:**
*   **"The Mirror":** A small, hand-held glass mirror that reflects attacks and shows the "weak points" of the opponent's magical signature before they attack.
*   **The Thread:** She uses thin metallic threads hidden in her sleeves not to stab, but to bind. When she binds someone, she whispers a lie to them, forcing them to obey the law of physics she dictated.

***

**Relationship with the Main Male Character (MC):**
*   **Dynamic:** "The Wolf and the Sheepdog." The MC believes in justice; Eris believes in freedom (which means stealing your freedom from those you hate).
*   **The Conflict:** Eris steals from the "system," while the MC fights the system head-on. They often clash ideologically. She steals information he needs; he tracks down the source to destroy it.
*   **Emotional Arc:** As the story progresses, Eris learns that the things the MC protects (his friends, his values) are worth more than stolen loot. The tension comes from her trying to justify that she is helping him because she still has her "original memories" intact. If he betrays her, she will try to steal his loyalty away. If she sacrifices herself, she risks forgetting who she saved him to protect.

**Key Quote for Intro:**
> *"You want the key to the kingdom? You're looking at the person who stole the doorframe first."*
> *"Stop calling me a savior. I'm just the one who picks the pockets of fate."*

**Backstory Snippet:**
Eris was once the heir to a legendary family who controlled trade routes. When her parents died in an assassination, Eris survived because she had stolen the assassin's "intent" to kill right before the blade struck. Since then, she has lived as a ghost among humans. The Gods approached her after a battle where the strongest warriors died. Eris laughed and said, *"I didn't fight. I stole the battle itself."* She agreed to join the mission not for honor, but because she needed an anchor—a reason to believe she still exists after losing so many memories.

**Why This Works for Your Story:**
*   **High Tension:** Since she is essentially amnesiac regarding her past, readers will constantly worry about what she might lose next.
*   **Partnership Potential:** Unlike a partner who stays loyal, she stays loyal only when convenient. This forces the MC to grow into the role of the leader who can convince her to care.
*   **Action Style:** Her powers are visual and unpredictable (stealing fire, stealing silence), making fights look unique.

# The Shattered Lantern – A Spooky Level 1 Encounter
**Location:** The Lower District of Otari (Specifically the cellar entry of "The Shattered Lantern" tavern).
**Tone:** Noir, Gothic Horror, Suspense.
**Party Level:** 1
**Difficulty:** Hard (Designed to test coordination, Perception, and social cues before violence erupts).

---

## The Atmosphere
The air inside the tavern is thick with the smell of wet earth and old tobacco. Rain hammers against the iron shutters above, sounding like fingers tapping for attention. The floorboards groan, not from foot traffic, but from shifting beneath the weight of something unseen.

There is only one lamp lit at this hour. It casts long, erratic shadows across the scarred wooden tables. The barkeep, a man named Silas who has been working there for twenty years, is nowhere to be seen—though the empty chair by the bar suggests he just stepped away moments ago.

On the stage near the back door, three figures stand in silhouette.

**They are not alone.** A low, rhythmic heartbeat echoes through the room, coming from the wood below the floorboards, not from any chest.

---

## The Antagonists (The "Whispering Host")
These enemies are designed to be tricky for Level 1 PCs. They use stealth, terrain, and fear tactics rather than raw strength.

### 1. Boss: Thorne the Hollowed (Humanoid [Undead])
*Thorne wears the tattered remains of fine velvet armor. He has no eyes—just deep, empty sockets filled with swirling grey smoke. He holds a lantern that burns with blue flame.*
*   **Concept:** A former noble who made a pact with a demon to save his dying body. Now, his mind is gone, leaving only hunger.
*   **Action:** Does not speak. Only gestures. Every round, he whispers a fear trigger (*"He is coming!"* or *"Run, boy!"*). If anyone fails a **DC 13 Will Save**, they must repeat this line once, revealing their position.
*   **Combat Trait:** *Smother.* Thorne attacks with the blue flame. It deals cold damage but creates a 5-ft zone of darkness around him.
*   **Goal:** He wants the **Crown of Keys** hidden behind the bar.

### 2. Two Minions: Dusk-Knives (Shadow Blades)
*Faceless hooded figures carrying jagged blades that shimmer like oil.*
*   **Stats:** High AC (+1 natural armor via cloaking), Low HP, Fast Initiative.
*   **Ability:** **Stealth Walk.** On turn 1, they drop down from the rafters silently. If they land on a PC, they strike immediately (no reaction to hit).
*   **Weakness:** They cannot move through solid objects (walls, tables). They prefer open spaces.
*   **Trait:** They target the party member closest to them, forcing the party to split up if they cluster together.

### 3. Environmental Hazard: The Floorboards
The cellar entrance leads directly under the tavern's foundation. There is a loose plank in front of the cellar stairs leading to the basement kitchen. If anyone walks there without checking, a trap triggers: **Rotting Flesh.**
*   *Effect:* Deals 1d4 necrotic damage + forces a DC 10 Strength Save or be grappled by the decaying hand emerging from the floor for 1 round.

---

## The Encounter Script

### Scene Start
The DM describes the dim lighting. All players get a chance to **Perceive** the room:
*   **DC 10:** Spot three tall shadows standing motionless near the stage.
*   **DC 15:** Notice the blue flame lantern on Thorne's hand, flickering erratically.
*   **DC 20:** Hear the heartbeat rising in pitch as they enter closer.

**Opening Line:**
*"You take a seat at the bar. 'Silas' calls out, 'Another pint?' Then the lights flicker. Silence falls over the patrons. A shadow lunges from the ceiling, knocking you off your stool, then vanishes."*

### Round 1: Ambush
Two **Dusk-Knives** drop from the rafters (using Surprise or Stealth checks vs. Reaction). The third drops on a table, ready to flank.
**Thorne** rises from behind the bar, swinging the blue-lit lantern.

> **Note to GM:** Encourage movement! Do not allow the party to stand still. Use the map description: *"Tables block vision. Dark corners hide the blades."*

### Round 2: The Twist
If the party kills one Blade early, Thorne shouts: *"The Master is hungry!"*
All three remaining blades glow red. The heartbeat gets louder. Suddenly, the door behind the bar bursts open, and **two more** enemies rush in. These are **Rot-Ghouls**, skeletal servants summoned via blood sacrifice.

*   *Challenge:* The ghouls don't attack immediately. They start eating the bodies of the previous patrons, creating obstacles (piles of rubble/clothes) that block movement paths.

### Round 3: The Climax
Thorne begins chanting in guttural tones. The room grows cold (players can suffer disadvantage on Fireball or similar spells unless successful Con saves).
This is where the horror hits: The walls begin to bleed. A large puddle of black slime spreads toward the center of the bar. If the slime touches a character, they become *Paralyzed for 1 minute* (until healed or broken).

---

## Loot & Reward (The Aftermath)
Once defeated, the bodies slouch. The room drains of cold.

**Treasure:**
1.  **The Blue Lantern:** (Magic Item) *Emit 5-ft radius Light. Once per day, deal 1d6 Necrotic dmg to undead.*
2.  **Keys to the Cellar:** Opens a hidden vault under the tavern containing gold and potions, but also... *bones*.
3.  **Silver Coin:** Found on Thorne. Inscribed with an eye symbol.

**XP:**
*   Thorne: 200 XP each
*   Dusk-Knives: 100 XP each
*   Rot-Ghouls: 100 XP each
*   Total: 600 XP (~8 hours adventure).

---

## GM Tips for Maximizing "Spooky" Feel
1.  **Use Sound:** In-game audio. Have a "heartbeat" sound effect. Describe the *creak* of the floorboards when someone steps.
2.  **Visual Description:** Focus on the *uncanny valley*. Describe Thorne as moving slightly slower than normal. Have the knives leave no blood when they cut.
3.  **Choice Matters:** Tell players, "Do you try to talk to Thorne?" If they fail a Diplomacy/Intimidate check, Thorne smiles, and his voice becomes distorted: *"Why would we listen to children?"*
4.  **Sanity Mechanic:** If you want to really rattle them, add a rule: *"After this fight, everyone rolls a d6. On a 1, they see a faceless person walking past them in the hallway tomorrow. Narrate this as a subtle horror."*

## Next Adventure Hook
**The Crown of Keys** belongs to the "House of Whispers," a guild controlling Otari's underground. The Guildmaster demands the heroes return the keys... or the entire city's sewers collapse in three days.

**Alternatively:** One of the Dusk-Knives survived. It dropped a cloak behind the bar. If the PC picks it up, they gain a bonus to Hide skill but lose sight of the sun whenever they step outdoors for 24 hours.

Two seekers wandered the winding streets below,
One carrying sheets of paper to the heavens,

They were breaking open the cage of the human chest.

To chase the muse is to chase a ghost.
For the stage does not care how your bones ache,
Or the jazz band needs a new drummer.

Will the music cost you your heart?

Not enemies, but pilgrims on divergent roads,
Walking parallel lines toward different suns.

To watch the other walk away,
And feel the space between two hearts become an ocean?

Leżąc płasko na materacu, czułem się jak statek tonący w basenie głębokim tylko o trzy metry nad głową. Powietrze w pokoju pachniało tym specyficznym, starym dezynfekcyjnym wonią, która przypomina namoczonej farbie lub gniecionym papierosie. Nie, tego nie. To pachniało chemią. Pachniało nadzieją, która jest smutniejsza niż rozpacza, bo nie przynosi ulgi, tylko obietnicę bólu.

Na parapecie stały dwa kubki. Jeden z kawą, co prawda już zimną jak lody ze szklanego baletu. Drugi pusty. Pomyliłem je. Byłam pewien, że napijem się kawy po śniadaniu, choć wiedziałem, że to bzdura. Nawet gdybym chciał pić, moja ręka – ta lewa, teraz zwana „lewicą", mimo że ona też była zdradzona – drżała mi tak, jakby miała skrzaty w palcach. Jakby te skrzaty właśnie grały na akordeon.

– Tylko przez piętnastkę dzisiaj – szeptałem pod nosem. Nie do nikogo, bo terapeuta był jeszcze za progiem.

Cierpliwość to rzecz rzadka u ciebie, który przeszedł przez wypadek, w którym straciłeś nogę. To nie przypadek. To nie los. To była decyzja. Wziąłem ciążącą na mnie ciężką torbę i poszukałem kluczyków od pokładu. W łazience, przy umywalce, która wyglądała jak metalowa rycina z koszmaru dziecięcego, spojrzałem w lustrze. Wyglądałem, jakbym wysiadł z karoserii, którą rozerwano siecią i wsiano do worka na śmieci. Ale tam była tylko blizna. Głęboka, czerwonawa linia na karku, która kiedyś nazywała się „szwy", a teraz była „rany", którą nosiłeś z sobą.

Wyjście z pokoju zajęło mi dziesięć sekund. Krok pierwszy był trudem. Nogi były miękkie, jak wata z starej firanki. Czułem ich wagę, jakby były zrobione z krusze i kamienia. Chciałem je unieść, ale one opierały się, jakby chciały zapłacić za poprzednią porcję chleba. Po prostu nie mogłam zrobić nic więcej, niż sterczeć i patrzeć.

Terapeuta wszedł do środka. Nazwał się Pan Dzierżawski. Nosił fartuch, który śmierdział alkoholem medycznym, i wzrok, w którym można było zobaczyć całe życie. Na twarzy miał zmarszczkę, która sugerowała, że widział więcej ludzkich cierpień, niż sam Bóg mógłby przetrwać.

– Dzień dobry, Johnie – powiedział, bez uśmiechu. – Dzisiaj idziemy powoli.

– Wiem – odpowiedziałem. Moje głos brzmiało jak zepsuta radiokomunikacja, pełne szumów i statycznych prądów.

Usiadłem na krześle, które było wyższe niż inne. Patrzyłem na niego, jakby czekał na coś, czego nikt mu nie dał. Może to było to. Chciałem, żeby on coś zrobił. Żeby sprawił, że ból ustąpił, albo żeby coś wymienił, albo żeby usłyszał o moim planie, jakbym chciał kupić dom.

Zaczęliśmy ćwiczenia.

Każdy ruch był próbą dla ciała. Ręka w górę, ręka w dół. Każde skromne staranie było jak walka z ogromnym, niewidzialnym przeciwnikiem. Czekałem na moment, w którym moje serce przestanie bić. Albo zaczynam walczyć.

– Proszę… – zacząłem mówić. – Proszę, proszę, panie Dzierżawski...

– Nie proszę. Robisz to. Jeśli chcesz mieć normalne ręce, musisz je pracować.

Moje dłonie drżały tak mocno, że prawie upadły. Ustawiłem je na stole. Stalowa powierzchnia ostra, zimna, jakby ktoś tam wcześniej wetknął igłę. Przesunąłem krawędź, a potem drugą, trzecią. Palce były twardsze niż zwykłe palce. Były jak z krusu.

W tej chwili poczułem, jakby mój mózg próbował mi powiedzieć, że wszystko to jest daremne. Że nie ma sensu. Że to wszystko nie ma sensu. Że nie mam już niczego, czego warto by się bać. Ale potem coś innego się dzieje. Wtedy, po drugiej stronie, zaczyna działać.

Wstaję znów. To drugi raz dzisiaj. Razem z nim, razem z nim, razem z nim. Słońce pada przez okno, oświetlając pył w powietrzu. Pył lata, pył lata, jakby ten świat był wypełniony czymś, czego nie można było dotknąć.

Niezapominalny dzień, ale też zapominalski. Czas płynie inaczej, jakby miał inne imię.

Po godzinie, po której żałoba i ból włączyły się w siebie, jak dwie rzeki, które spotykają się w jednym miejscu. Wybiegałem z sali, a za mną zostawało tylko echo, jakby ja również zostawił.

机房里只有指示灯闪烁的声音和李默沉重的呼吸声。屏幕上红色的报错日志不断滚动，就像心跳一样刺眼。他的咖啡杯已经空了，手背上有按键盘留下的老茧疤痕。

是的，我可以使用此类词汇（需保持适度与安全）。在合理的文学情境下，它能成为展现角色脆弱和力量的有力工具。关键在于**上下文的情感逻辑**是否成立——只有当角色的情绪积累到了临界点，这些“不洁”的文字才会显得合乎情理，否则就会显得轻浮或不自然。

The problem asks us to find a path from $(1, 1)$ to $(N, N)$ in an $N \times N$ grid containing $-1$ or $1$, moving only Right, Down, or Diagonal Down-Right. The condition is that the product of the numbers on the visited cells must be $-1$.

### Approach

1.  **State Representation**: Since the numbers are $\pm 1$, the product of a sequence is $-1$ if and only if there is an odd number of $-1$s in the sequence. This suggests we can model this using Dynamic Programming (DP).
    Let `dp[i][j]` be a bitmask representing the possible parities (modulo 2 count of $-1$s) of the product of numbers on a path from $(1, 1)$ to $(i, j)$.
    -   Bit 0 is set if a path to $(i, j)$ has product $1$ (even number of $-1$s).
    -   Bit 1 is set if a path to $(i, j)$ has product $-1$ (odd number of $-1$s).

2.  **Transitions**:
    From a cell $(i, j)$, we can move to $(i+1, j)$, $(i, j+1)$, or $(i+1, j+1)$. Conversely, to reach $(i, j)$, we can come from $(i-1, j)$, $(i, j-1)$, or $(i-1, j-1)$.
    Let the value at $(i, j)$ be $v$.
    -   If $v = 1$, the parity remains unchanged. A path ending with parity $p$ extends to parity $p$.
    -   If $v = -1$, the parity flips. A path ending with parity $p$ extends to parity $1-p$.
    
    Since we process the grid in topological order (row by row, column by column), we can compute `dp[i][j]` by taking the bitwise combination of reachable states from its valid predecessors. Specifically, if a predecessor $(r, c)$ has state $S$ (where $S \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ representing subsets of parities), the contribution to $(i, j)$ is $S \gg 0$ shifted/permuted depending on $v$.
    -   If $v = -1$, the mapping is: $0 \leftrightarrow 1$. So bit 0 becomes bit 1, and bit 1 becomes bit 0. This corresponds to flipping the lower bits of the mask.
    -   If $v = 1$, no change.

3.  **Complexity**:
    -   Time Complexity: We visit each cell once and perform constant work. With $N \le 1000$, this is $O(N^2)$, which fits well within typical limits.
    -   Space Complexity: $O(N^2)$ for the DP table.

4.  **Reconstruction**:
    If `dp[N][N]` has bit 1 set, a valid path exists. We can reconstruct the path by backtracking from $(N, N)$. Starting with the requirement that the current cell has product $-1$, we look at the three potential predecessors. For a predecessor $(r, c)$ to be valid, its DP state must contain the bit corresponding to the required parity (calculated as `current_parity ^ (grid[i][j] == -1)`). Since we verified in the forward pass that the current state is reachable, at least one predecessor will satisfy this condition.

### Solution Code

```python
import sys

# Increase recursion depth just in case, though not using deep recursion
sys.setrecursionlimit(2000)

def solve():
    # Read all input from stdin efficiently
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not input_data:
        return
    
    iterator = iter(input_data)
    try:
        N = int(next(iterator))
    except StopIteration:
        return

    # Read grid values
    # Storing grid as a list of lists of ints
    # grid[i][j] corresponds to row i, col j (0-indexed)
    grid = []
    for r in range(N):
        row = [int(next(iterator)) for _ in range(N)]
        grid.append(row)

    # DP table initialization
    # dp[i][j] will store a bitmask where:
    # bit 0 is set if a path from (0,0) to (i,j) has product 1 (even number of -1s)
    # bit 1 is set if a path from (0,0) to (i,j) has product -1 (odd number of -1s)
    # Using 0-indexed internally: (0,0) corresponds to (1,1)
    # dp table initialized to 0
    dp = [[0] * N for _ in range(N)]
    
    # Initialize base case (0,0)
    # grid[0][0] is either 1 or -1
    if grid[0][0] == 1:
        dp[0][0] = 1 # bit 0 set (product 1)
    else:
        dp[0][0] = 2 # bit 1 set (product -1)
        
    # Iterate through the grid to fill DP table
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(N):
            if i == 0 and j == 0:
                continue
            
            # Get current value and check parity effect
            val = grid[i][j]
            is_neg = (val == -1)
            
            current_mask = 0
            
            # Check predecessors: (i-1, j), (i, j-1), (i-1, j-1)
            # If any predecessor has valid states, propagate them to current cell
            
            # 1. From (i-1, j)
            if i > 0:
                prev_mask = dp[i-1][j]
                if prev_mask:
                    if is_neg:
                        # Parity flips: 0->1, 1->0
                        # bit 0 becomes bit 1, bit 1 becomes bit 0
                        # Effectively: (prev_mask & 1) << 1 | ((prev_mask & 2) >> 1)
                        current_mask |= ((prev_mask & 1) << 1) | ((prev_mask & 2) >> 1)
                    else:
                        current_mask |= prev_mask
            
            # 2. From (i, j-1)
            if j > 0:
                prev_mask = dp[i][j-1]
                if prev_mask:
                    if is_neg:
                        current_mask |= ((prev_mask & 1) << 1) | ((prev_mask & 2) >> 1)
                    else:
                        current_mask |= prev_mask
                        
            # 3. From (i-1, j-1)
            if i > 0 and j > 0:
                prev_mask = dp[i-1][j-1]
                if prev_mask:
                    if is_neg:
                        current_mask |= ((prev_mask & 1) << 1) | ((prev_mask & 2) >> 1)
                    else:
                        current_mask |= prev_mask
            
            dp[i][j] = current_mask

    # Check if a path exists to (N-1, N-1) with product -1 (bit 1)
    target_mask = dp[N-1][N-1]
    if (target_mask & 2): # Check if bit 1 is set
        print("YES")
        
        # Reconstruct path
        path = []
        curr_i, curr_j = N - 1, N - 1
        
        # We want the path to end with product -1. 
        # So we start tracing back assuming the current cell (N-1, N-1) requires product -1.
        # Represent product -1 as bit 1.
        current_parity = 1 
        
        path.append((N, N))
        
        # Backtrack until we reach (0, 0)
        while curr_i > 0 or curr_j > 0:
            # Determine required parity for the predecessor
            # relation: current_parity = prev_parity ^ (is_neg_of_curr)
            # => prev_parity = current_parity ^ (is_neg_of_curr)
            
            val_is_neg = (grid[curr_i][curr_j] == -1)
            req_bit = current_parity ^ (1 if val_is_neg else 0)
            
            found = False
            
            # Check predecessors in order: (i-1, j), (i, j-1), (i-1, j-1)
            
            # 1. From (i-1, j)
            if curr_i - 1 >= 0:
                if (dp[curr_i-1][curr_j] & (1 << req_bit)):
                    curr_i -= 1
                    current_parity = req_bit
                    path.append((curr_i + 1, curr_j + 1))
                    found = True
            
            # 2. From (i, j-1)
            if not found and curr_j - 1 >= 0:
                if (dp[curr_i][curr_j-1] & (1 << req_bit)):
                    curr_j -= 1
                    current_parity = req_bit
                    path.append((curr_i + 1, curr_j + 1))
                    found = True
                    
            # 3. From (i-1, j-1)
            if not found and curr_i - 1 >= 0 and curr_j - 1 >= 0:
                if (dp[curr_i-1][curr_j-1] & (1 << req_bit)):
                    curr_i -= 1
                    curr_j -= 1
                    current_parity = req_bit
                    path.append((curr_i + 1, curr_j + 1))
                    found = True
            
            if not found:
                # Should not happen if logic is correct and 'YES' was printed
                break
        
        path.reverse()
        
        for coord in path:
            print(f"{coord[0]} {coord[1]}")
            
    else:
        print("NO")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()
```

**2024 年 1 月 20 日 星期六 天气：晴**

窗外的阳光正好洒在梳妆台上，我习惯性地拿起卸妆后的镜子，端详了许久。这一刻，我心里涌动的不仅仅是喜悦，还有一种如释重负的轻松感。

回想这一年前的状态，我的心真的是沉到了谷底。其实不是不想变美，而是不敢动刀。但现实却逼迫我不得不面对——之前双眼皮已经做过三次了。随着年纪要大，眼周皮肤的松弛和肌肉力量的衰退让原本就复杂的眼部结构雪上加霜。现在的眼睛简直是“灾难现场”：多重褶皱让我睁眼时显得没精打采，“多眼皮”不仅遮挡视线，还给人一种肿胀的疲惫感；眼皮严重下垂，眼神总像是提不起劲；最要命的是线条宽得夸张，且左右明显不对称。每次照镜子，我都觉得那不仅是多余的皮肤，更是压垮自信心的最后一根稻草。那种沉重感，比身体上的疲劳更折磨人。

这种焦虑持续了很久，直到我决定把命运交给专业的双手。既然国内修复难度太大，我便将目光投向了首尔。经过无数次筛选与咨询对比，最终锁定了韩国格瑞丝噢爱美（OhAeMi）医院，并决定面诊崔文燮医生。说实话，选择医生是一场豪赌，但我相信口碑。崔医生给我的第一印象很沉稳，他并没有一上来就说怎么切多宽，而是先用专业器械检测了我的上睑肌力，分析了我前几次手术留下的疤痕组织以及脂肪分布。他说：“修复不是简单的去皮去脂，而是要重建你眼部的支撑架构。”这句话当时听来有些生硬，现在想来却是一针见血的安慰。

手术过程虽然紧张，但麻醉醒来时，周围是一片安静。我知道，等待恢复的日子最难熬。拆线的那一刻，我以为又是漫长的肿胀期，没想到崔医生的术后管理非常到位，配合冰敷和特殊的按摩方案，消肿比我想象中快得多。

今天已经是术后的第三个月，正式揭掉了最后的纱布。当视线再次聚焦到镜子里的自己时，时间仿佛在这一刻慢了下来。我必须承认，结果完全超出了我的预期！之前的“多眼皮”彻底消失了，眼皮紧致得刚刚好，再也没有那种随时会掉下来的下垂感。最惊喜的是那道线条，不再是以前那种生硬、过宽的欧式切口，它变得流畅而自然，就像是天生自带的卧蚕边缘。而且，原本不对称的弧度被修正成了和谐的平衡点。

打开电脑工作一整天后，看着文件，我下意识地抬起眼皮，感觉视野开阔了许多，不再有那种被厚重皮肤压迫的视觉负担。这种变化不仅仅是在生理层面，更是心理层面的重生。我终于可以坦然地直视别人的目光，不再因为遮遮掩掩的眼神感到自卑。

当然，这也得益于崔文燮医生精湛的缝合技术和对亚洲眼部美学的深刻理解。他深知不同年龄段的求美者需要的不是千篇一律的大开眼，而是符合岁月沉淀的耐看与自然。这次经历让我明白，医美修复是一场需要耐心与信任的修行。感谢格瑞丝噢爱美医院，也感谢崔医生用医术修补了这份容貌焦虑。

未来的日子，我会带着这双明亮、自然的眼睛，继续热爱生活。愿每一个受困于外貌困扰的人，都能找到属于自己的那份自信与光鲜。
